extracted.intended_audience: current and prospective NEH Summer Stipends applicants and individual award recipients (individual scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Terms and conditions governing acceptance, administration, allowable activities, payments, travel, reporting, compliance, and closeout for NEH Summer Stipend awards issued prior to Jan 1, 2025. Covers recipient obligations, restrictions, and government-wide requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of institutional affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have an academic institutional affiliation, NEH requires you to notify your department chair, chief academic officer, and director of sponsored research that NEH has offered you an award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance via eGMS Reach
rubrics_metrics.description: To accept the award, you must complete and submit the NEH Individual Program Acceptance Form through eGMS Reach, NEH's online grant management system, by the deadline indicated in your offer letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The acceptance form is in the Forms & Reports tab of your offer in eGMS Reach; learn how to access eGMS Reach via NEH guidance; contact Summer Stipends Program for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient overall responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In accepting an NEH award, you, as the recipient, have full responsibility for conducting approved project activities, adhering to these terms and conditions, and informing the NEH during the course of the award of any significant issues that arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH relies on separation of responsibilities within its staff; recipients must comply with statutes, regulations, and NEH policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH roles and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH Office of Grant Management oversees compliance with administrative requirements and is the only office authorized to issue the notice of award; NEH program officers handle programmatic aspects; Office of Accounting handles ACH/payment processing; Office of Inspector General handles audits/investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Grant Management negotiates awards, interprets federal award policies, and performs post-award monitoring; contact Inspector General to report fraud or misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment (two consecutive months full-time)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to devote two consecutive months of full-time work to the project described in your summer stipend application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not accept a teaching assignment or undertake any activities that divert you from your summer stipend project during the period of performance. Summer stipends normally support work carried out during the summer months, but arrangements can be made for holding tenure at other times of the year if requested and approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting alternate period of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you desire an award period of performance that falls outside the period from May 1 to September 30, send a request by email explaining the circumstances to the Summer Stipends Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Summer Stipends Program staff by email or phone to discuss exceptional scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent (non-NEH) funding allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: You may hold other, non-NEH sources of support (e.g., sabbaticals and supplemental funding) or grants for the same project as your NEH-supported project during your summer stipend period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH summer stipends require continuous, full-time work. In some cases there are additional restrictions; contact staff before accepting other funding if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on multiple NEH individual awards
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not accept or hold more than one NEH individual award (e.g., Fellowship, Public Scholar, or Summer Stipend) in a given fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction regarding NEH institutional awards
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not work on a project supported by an NEH institutional award as either a project director or participant while holding an NEH Summer Stipend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work toward degrees prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: You may audit courses and seminars pertinent to your Summer Stipend project, but you may not enroll in a degree program or engage in work you intend to apply toward a degree either now or later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of NEH in products
rubrics_metrics.description: All materials resulting from activities accomplished under an award (e.g., books or articles) must contain an acknowledgment of NEH support, and include the specified disclaimer: “Any views, findings, conclusions, or recommendations expressed in the (publication) (program) (website) do not necessarily reflect those of the National Endowment for the Humanities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NEH publicizing-your-project guidance for media tips and suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment procedures — ACH form required
rubrics_metrics.description: The ACH form (SF 3881) allows NEH to transfer funds to your or your employer’s account; NEH cannot pay you until you submit this form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may elect deposit to personal or employer account. If you choose employer account, complete payee info with employer banking info but enter your social security number. You need submit the form only once unless banking changes. Do not attach payment requests to eGMS Reach messages or emails to NEH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment — bank routing and account number guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Routing and account numbers must be provided correctly; a sample check graphic is provided. Do not use deposit slips to obtain routing/account info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tip: If the first two digits of the routing number are not 01–12, 21–32, or 61–72 the direct deposit will be rejected. If the check is payable through a different bank, contact your financial institution for the correct routing number. Checking account number can be up to 17 digits (no letters); include hyphens but omit spaces and special symbols; do not include the check number. Funds must be transferred directly to a checking or savings account; funds cannot be transferred to a trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal debt — no delinquency
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not be delinquent in the repayment of any federal debt. Should you become delinquent during your period of performance, you must notify NEH immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH will not release award funds until you provide evidence that you have entered into a repayment agreement with the IRS and that you are current on all payments due. Examples include student loans, delinquent federal taxes, delinquent child support, and delinquent payroll taxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment definition and Buy American encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment is defined as tangible, nonexpendable personal property having a useful life of more than one year and an acquisition cost of $5,000 or more per unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with Executive Order 13788, if you purchase equipment and products costing $10,000 or more per unit with NEH funds, you should purchase only American-made equipment and products. This encouragement does not apply to commercial information technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fringe benefits or insurance provided
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH provides neither medical insurance nor any other fringe benefits for awardees. NEH awards to individuals do not cover unemployment compensation and Social Security insurance because recipients are not employees of the U.S. Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consider continuing any benefit programs in which they are participating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income tax — NEH does not withhold or provide tax advice
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH does not and cannot provide tax advice. NEH does not withhold Social Security, State or federal income taxes from your award. NEH does not send 1099s or other tax forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct specific questions regarding taxability to the IRS, appropriate state/local officials, or your tax advisor. The IRS interactive tax assistant addresses whether scholarships/fellowships/education grants should be included as income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic airfare limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Airfare for domestic travel charged to the award may not exceed the value of the basic least expensive unrestricted accommodations class offered by commercial airlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: International travel documentation and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: You are responsible to secure necessary passports, visas, licenses, permits, and approvals prior to undertaking activities outside the United States and must notify NEH if a permit is denied or revoked or if unforeseen circumstances threaten or prevent project activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH does not assume responsibility for your compliance with laws of the country where you conduct work. NEH encourages registration with State Department’s STEP for travel alerts and easier embassy contact in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign travel airfare limitation and Fly America Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Airfare for foreign travel paid with NEH funds may not exceed the value of the basic least expensive unrestricted accommodations class. In accordance with the Fly America Act (49 U.S.C. 40118), all air transportation paid in whole or part with NEH funds must be performed on a U.S. flag air carrier, except in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible exceptions include: transportation under a U.S./foreign 'Open Skies' Agreement when allowed; involuntary rerouting via a foreign carrier; specific circumstances where use of a non-U.S. carrier eliminates changes or greatly reduces travel time; short distance travel (≤3 hours elapsed flight time) where foreign carrier is permissible; and other narrowly specified cases. Lower cost, convenience, or traveler preference are NOT acceptable reasons for using a foreign air carrier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on political and social advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH funds may not be used for promotion of a particular political, religious, or ideological point of view; advocacy for a particular program of social or political action; or support of specific public policies or legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also the Prohibition on the Use of Funds for Lobbying Activities (Byrd Anti-Lobbying Amendment, 31 U.S.C. 1352, and 18 U.S.C. 1913).

rubrics_metrics.name: No changes without prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not change your project scope, work plan, period of performance or the due date of your reporting requirements without prior NEH approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests for changes must be submitted through eGMS Reach (Changes Requests tab). Scope/work plan amendments must describe and justify proposed changes and be submitted as soon as possible but no later than 30 days prior to end of period of performance. Period of performance and report due date change requests must be submitted at least 30 days prior to the relevant deadline. Amendment requests are considered case-by-case and approval is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final performance report requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a final performance report on activities accomplished with your NEH award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report due within 120 days if you received your award on or after November 12, 2020; if before that date the final report is due within 90 days of the end of your period of performance. Submit electronically via eGMS Reach. A final financial report is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of award products to NEH
rubrics_metrics.description: One copy of all award products should be forwarded to NEH as soon as they are available, no matter how long after grant completion the publication may appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to maintain a record of all documents pertinent to your award for a period of three years from the date you submit your Final Performance Report to the NEH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and NEH reproduction rights
rubrics_metrics.description: You may copyright any work developed under your NEH award. NEH reserves a royalty-free, non-exclusive, and irrevocable right to reproduce, publish, or otherwise use your NEH-supported work for federal purposes, and to authorize others to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH has typically exercised this right in consultation with recipients to publish an excerpt in Humanities Magazine or on the NEH website. NEH may also make available narrative and bibliography submitted with your application under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for Library of Congress Cataloging in Publication (CIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH strongly recommends that you catalog any publication that results from this award under the Cataloging in Publication (CIP) Program of the Library of Congress before final printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIP enables libraries to acquire and process books quickly; publishers ineligible for CIP may be eligible for Preassigned Card Number Program. Entering titles in national bibliographic databases increases dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Humanities Council notification
rubrics_metrics.description: You must notify your state humanities council of your award and, wherever possible, give advance notice of any related public events occurring in the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of state humanities councils is available on NEH's website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct policy adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will take appropriate action against individuals and organizations upon a determination that misconduct has occurred in proposing, performing, or reviewing research or reporting results from research activities funded by NEH in accordance with the NEH Research Misconduct Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of funds for lobbying activities (Byrd Anti-Lobbying Amendment and 18 U.S.C. 1913)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not use appropriated funds to influence the Executive or Legislative Branches of the federal government in connection with a specific award, and may not use funds for certain electioneering, political party support, attempts to influence legislation, or some legislative liaison activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH must include text of 18 U.S.C. 1913 in award documents. Violations may constitute criminal or statutory offenses under cited laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug-Free Workplace Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 (2 CFR part 3373) and may not engage in unlawful manufacture, distribution, dispensing, possession, or use of a controlled substance in conducting any grant activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If convicted of a criminal drug offense resulting from a violation occurring during grant activities, you must report the conviction in writing to the Office of Grants Management within ten calendar days and include the federal award identification number of each affected award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with labor standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must comply with the labor standards set out in Labor Standards on Projects or Productions Assisted by Grants from the National Endowments for the Arts and Humanities (see 29 CFR part 505).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination for discontinuance or nonobservance
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH may terminate your Summer Stipend if you choose to discontinue the proposed program before the end of the period of performance or fail to observe the award’s terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you discontinue the program early you must return any funds received over and above those to which you are entitled. If unable to meet the terms during performance, inform NEH immediately; advance stipend payments may require repayment of a portion, and NEH will inform you of amount, basis for calculation, and repayment date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debarment and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not be debarred, suspended, proposed for debarment, declared ineligible, or voluntarily excluded from participation in covered transactions by any federal department or agency; nor within the three years preceding application have been convicted of or had civil judgment for specified offenses related to public transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified offenses include fraud, antitrust violations, embezzlement, theft, forgery, bribery, falsification/destruction of records, making false statements, receiving stolen property, having public transactions terminated for cause, or being presently indicted or charged. See 2 CFR Parts 180 and 3369. Debarment will result in immediate termination of the award.
